articles.title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
articles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers
articles.summary: Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

articles.title: MCP C# SDK 2.0 Makes HTTP Stateless by Default and Adds Multi Round-Trip Requests
articles.author: Edin Kapić
articles.summary: Microsoft announced version 2.0 of the official MCP C# SDK, which implements the 2026-07-28 revision of the Model Context Protocol with stateless HTTP servers by default, standardised routing headers and Multi Round-Trip Requests. Releases 2.1 to 2.3 have since added hybrid session serving, a subscriptions/listen handler and a series of discovery, OAuth and shutdown fixes. By Edin Kapić

articles.title: AGNTCon + MCPCon 2026: Agentic AI Foundation Adds Four Projects as MCP Turns to Security

articles.summary: At AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2026, the Agentic AI Foundation added OpenSandbox, Open Responses, Agent Skills, and OpenEnv, reaching ten projects in its first year. Keynotes from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and UC Berkeley focused on MCP in production, security, and agents with their own identities. By Andrew Hoblitzell

articles.title: Article: The Evolution of Agentic Harnesses: From Chains to Graph to Code
articles.author: Karthik Ramgopal
articles.summary: Agentic LLM systems have moved from linear prompt chains to graph-based workflows and, more recently, code-executing harnesses. Chains are simple but fragile, graphs add branching, retries, and validation, and code harnesses verify outputs through execution. The article advises validating model outputs and choosing the least complex design that meets reliability, speed, and cost needs. By Karthik Ramgopal
